chunks: Abū Baṣīr narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said:

There is no harm in giving the adhān while riding, or walking, or without wudu (ablution). But do not perform the iqāmah while you are riding or sitting, unless due to an excuse, or if you are on slippery ground.

key_terms.تُؤَذِّنَ: to recite the adhān, the call announcing salat (prayer)
key_terms.تُقِمْ: to recite the iqāmah, the second call immediately before salat (prayer)
key_terms.عُذْرٍ: a valid excuse or legally recognized impediment
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution required for states of taharah

ai.seo_question: Can a person give the adhān or iqāmah while riding, walking, sitting, or without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the adhān and iqāmah. It permits the adhān in less formal states such as while riding, walking, or without wudu (ablution), but requires greater formality for the iqāmah unless there is an excuse or difficult ground conditions.
